explanation.en: The Attorney General's summary says covered assets exclude real property and "some pensions and retirement accounts"; the Analyst says they "generally would be excluded". The text of Proposition 40 exempts qualified pensions and individual retirement arrangements, and Roth-type retirement accounts except to the extent the aggregate value in all of them exceeds $10 million. So most retirement accounts are excluded, but Roth-type amounts above $10 million would be counted. Whether this would be the first California tax on retirement accounts is not addressed in the guide.
